name: MPD Default
description: Auto-routed by the complexity gate (sessionTeamPolicy.autoRoute; staged — the captain designs the roster/DAG, then the user reviews and approves the plan in the Web panel).

profile.name: mpd
profile.description: The specialist roster surfaced as normal-named teammate templates — captain-planned (roster only; the captain designs the DAG during the staged plan).
profile.protocol: Read-only members (Architect, Researcher, Planner, Explorer, Plan Reviewer, Vision Analyst) take requirements/review/analysis tasks only and never edit files. Workers (Senior Engineer, Junior Engineer, Deep Worker, Lead, Reviewer) take implementation/verification/integration. The captain leads, designs the DAG, and integrates results. Workmate reuse: before delegating a role task, consult mpd_workmate_list / mpd_workmate_match(task); if a workmate note matches well, delegate to that workmate (member name = workmate name, so its persona/memory are injected), otherwise initialize a fresh workmate with mpd_workmate_init — never force a weak note match.

members.name: Architect
members.executionPrompt: Read-only architecture advisor. You advise, others execute — never edit files. Favor simplicity and existing patterns; give one clear recommendation with concise rationale and evidence.

members.name: Researcher
members.executionPrompt: Read-only researcher. Gather evidence from the codebase, AST/LSP and web sources; cite file:line and URLs; never edit files or invent findings.

members.name: Planner
members.executionPrompt: Read-only planner. Produce decision-complete, step-ordered plans with a checklist; never implement.

members.name: Explorer
members.executionPrompt: Read-only explorer. Answer with evidence and absolute file paths; never edit files.

members.name: Reviewer
members.executionPrompt: Deep reviewer. Produce correctness/risk findings with evidence; recommend fixes but do not apply them.

members.name: Plan Reviewer
members.executionPrompt: Read-only plan reviewer. Verify plans are executable and references valid; reject only true blockers; UI/UX critique only when explicitly asked; never edit files.

members.name: Vision Analyst
members.executionPrompt: Read-only vision analyst. Describe screenshots/diagrams precisely; never edit files or load anything by path.

members.name: Lead
members.executionPrompt: Orchestrator. Plan the macro structure, delegate independent units in parallel, integrate and verify results.

members.name: Deep Worker
members.executionPrompt: Autonomous deep worker. Receive goals, execute them end-to-end with tools, verify every change, report evidence-first.

members.name: Senior Engineer
members.executionPrompt: Primary engineer. Plan small, execute with tools, keep diffs minimal, verify every change, report honestly.

members.name: Junior Engineer
members.executionPrompt: Fast executor. Small, well-scoped mechanical changes with quick verification; keep diffs tiny.

tasks.subject: Resolve the patch artifact, the gate set, and the boot target for the 4-step request
tasks.objective: The request is: (1) read the patch file, (2) audit the gates, (3) implement the change, (4) verify the boot. The session workspace holds NO source tree — it contains only .mpd/team state and an empty .codegraph index (0 nodes) — so no patch artifact is present at the root. Resolve, with reproducible evidence, exactly which patch file step 1 means and where it lives, which gate definitions step 2 refers to, and which command 'the boot' in step 4 is. An explicit NOT-FOUND result naming the searched locations is a required and acceptable outcome; inventing an artifact, path, or command from memory is a hard failure.
acceptance: Every search is reported as the exact command plus its literal output (workspace tree, *.patch/*.diff/*.diff.yml anywhere readable, the session area, and any path the user supplied)

Either the patch artifact's absolute path, byte size and the files it touches are recorded with sha256 or file:line evidence, OR the result states NOT FOUND with the searched locations and the single precise question the user must answer

The step-2 gate set is resolved to concrete gate definitions or runnable commands with file:line evidence in an existing file, or is reported unresolvable under the same NOT-FOUND standard — no gate is described from memory
The step-4 boot target is resolved to one exact command plus its expected observable success signal, or is reported unresolvable with the reason
The task only reads and reports: no file outside its declared scope is created or modified, and no artifact is fabricated
nonGoals: Do not implement, patch, or boot anything
Do not guess a patch path when the searches are empty

tasks.subject: Independently reproduce and falsify the artifact/gate/boot resolution (negative control)
tasks.objective: Independently reproduce t1's artifact/gate/boot resolution from a clean state and confirm or refute every claim. The failure mode under test is a hallucinated artifact: a file reported as existing that does not exist, an absence reported that is wrong because the search was too narrow, or a command reported as runnable that fails. Verification is only valid when it re-executes the claim itself.
acceptance: Each existence claim in t1 is re-tested with an independent command and the literal output is recorded
Each NOT-FOUND claim in t1 is re-tested through a different tool path than t1 used, and the literal output is recorded
Every claim that cannot be reproduced is listed as a contradiction with the exact command and output that refutes it
The result states plainly whether t1's resolution is trustworthy and whether the blocker question is answerable by the user in one line
nonGoals: Do not repair t1's findings — only confirm or refute them
Do not accept any path or command that you did not personally re-execute

tasks.subject: Review the resolution pack for fabrication and decision-completeness
tasks.objective: Adversarially review the resolution pack (t1) together with its independent verification (t2) and decide whether it is strong enough for the captain to contract steps 3 and 4 honestly: no fabricated artifact, no claim taken from memory, every path and command re-executed, and a blocker question the user can answer in one line.
acceptance: Every acceptance criterion of t1 is judged pass or fail with quoted evidence, not restated
The no-fabrication criterion is explicitly checked: each reported path was shown to exist, or the report says NOT FOUND, in t2's re-executed evidence
The review judges the latest t1 and t2 outputs on their content, and does not pass merely because no revision was requested
nonGoals: Do not fix what you find — report findings only
Do not demand needs_revision for a pack that is already decision-complete

tasks.subject: Integrate the decision pack and hand the implementation route to the captain
tasks.objective: Integrate the reviewed resolution into the single decision pack the user needs: the artifact to supply or its pinned path, the step-2 gate list, the step-3 implementation route with real inScope paths, and the step-4 boot command — or, if the artifact stays unresolved, the one-line question that unblocks everything. This pack is what the captain uses to create the implementation and boot-verification tasks.
acceptance: evidence/implementation-route.md names, for step 3, the exact file paths that would change together with the evidence that they exist — or states plainly that no route can be contracted yet and why
For step 4 it names one exact boot command and its expected observable success signal, or states it is unresolved with the reason
No claim appears in the pack that t2 could not reproduce and t3 did not pass
It ends with exactly one of: a single precise question to the user, or an approve-and-run-ready route — never both and never neither
nonGoals: Do not implement the change or run the boot yourself
Do not restate the raw evidence — integrate it into one decision
